base_uri.description: Base URL path for the Monitorix web interface (e.g., '/monitorix'). Must start with a slash.

http_host.description: IP address or hostname to bind the HTTP server to. Use '0.0.0.0' for all interfaces.

http_port.description: TCP port on which the Monitorix HTTP server listens.

use_internal_server.description: Whether to use Monitorix’s built-in HTTP server (true) or rely on a reverse proxy (false).

template_dir.description: Absolute path to directory containing HTML templates for rendering graphs.

data_dir.description: Directory where RRD database files and other persistent data are stored.

pid_file.description: Path to the PID file for the Monitorix daemon.

log_file.description: Path to the log file. Use '-' to log to standard output (useful for systemd).

log_level.description: Verbosity of logging: 0 = quiet, 1 = errors only, 2 = warnings, 3 = info (recommended for production).

lang.description: Default language for the UI labels and messages (Monitorix supports 'en', 'de', 'es', 'fr', 'pt_BR', 'ru').

interval.description: Interval in seconds between each data collection cycle (minimum 5, typical values: 60–300).

history_hours.description: Number of hours of historical data to retain in the RRD database (12–720 typical).

mysql_enabled.description: Enable monitoring of MySQL/MariaDB server statistics.

mysql_user.description: MySQL username for monitoring (requires REPLICATION CLIENT/SLAVE MONITOR privileges).

mysql_password.description: MySQL password for the monitoring user. Leave empty for socket auth (recommended).

mysql_socket.description: MySQL socket path — used instead of host/port if provided.

monitored_services.description: List of systemd services to monitor (name, enabled toggle, and unit name).

name.description: Friendly display name for the service.

enabled.description: Whether to enable monitoring for this service.

description.description: Optional human-readable description (defaults to unit name if omitted).

monitored_ports.description: List of TCP/UDP ports to monitor for listening status.

name.description: Friendly display name for the port.

monitored_filesystems.description: Filesystems to monitor for disk usage and I/O stats.

monitored_interfaces.description: Network interfaces to monitor for traffic and error counters.

monitored_processes.description: Processes to monitor by name pattern (e.g., 'nginx', 'python3').

name.description: Display name for the process group.

enabled.description: Whether to monitor processes matching this pattern.

pattern.description: Process name or regex pattern (as seen in 'ps aux').

webserver_enabled.description: Enable monitoring of Apache or Nginx status pages (e.g., mod_status or stub_status).

webserver_url.description: URL to the server-status endpoint (must end with '?auto' for Apache).

webserver_user.description: HTTP Basic auth username (if required by the status endpoint).

smart_enabled.description: Enable SMART disk monitoring (requires smartmontools and appropriate permissions).

smart_devices.description: List of disk devices (e.g., ['/dev/sda', '/dev/sdb']) to monitor SMART attributes for.

items.description: Device path for a SMART-capable disk.
